cards.text: Jesus comes back to the rest of His disciples and finds a large crowd around them, with scribes arguing with them. You leave the group chat for ONE afternoon and come back to four hundred messages.

cards.question: As soon as all the people in that crowd see Jesus, how do they react?

answers.text: They're filled with awe and run to greet Him
They go quiet and slowly back away from Him
They keep on arguing and pay Him no mind

cards.text: Jesus asks, "What are you disputing with them?" Whole debate going, and the one who answers is a dad in the crowd: "Teacher, I brought You my son…"

cards.question: The dad says his son has a spirit that makes him ___.

cards.text: Whenever the spirit seizes the boy, it throws him to the ground, and he foams at the mouth, gnashes his teeth and becomes rigid. I bet that never gets easier for a dad to say out loud.

cards.question: The dad asked Jesus' disciples to drive the spirit out, but they were ___.

cards.text: Jesus replies, "O unbelieving generation!" He asks how long He must remain with them and put up with them, and if I was one of those disciples, I'd be studying my sandals REAL hard right now.

cards.question: Right after calling them an unbelieving generation, what does Jesus tell them to do?
When they bring the boy, the spirit sees Jesus and immediately throws the boy into a convulsion.
Jesus asks the boy's father how long this has been with him. The dad says it only started recently.

cards.text: Friend, this dad has been carrying this a LONG time: the spirit often throws his son into the fire or into the water, trying to kill him. Then he says, "But if You can do anything, have compassion on us and help us."

cards.question: Jesus echoes part of the dad's request right back at him. Which part?
Then Jesus tells the dad that all things are possible to him who ___.

cards.text: Immediately the boy's father cries out, no speech and no polish. That man skips the small talk like his phone's on 1%.

cards.question: When the boy's father cries out to Jesus, what does he say about his own faith?

answers.text: He believes and asks for help with his unbelief
He has always believed without a single doubt
He doesn't believe at all and needs a sign

cards.text: When Jesus sees that a crowd has come running, He rebukes the unclean spirit and calls it what it is, a deaf and mute spirit. Friend, when somebody calls you by your FULL title, you already know how this ends.

cards.question: Jesus commands the deaf and mute spirit to come out of the boy and never ___ him again.

cards.text: That spirit does NOT leave quietly: it shrieks, convulses the boy violently, and then it's out. The boy becomes like a corpse, so that many say, "He is dead."

cards.question: While the boy lies there like a corpse, Jesus takes him by the hand and helps him to his feet.
Later in the house, the disciples ask Jesus privately why they couldn't drive the spirit out. What does Jesus say this kind can only come out by?

findings.problem: Mark 9:14 starts mid-thought: "When they returned." The opening card says only that Jesus comes back. It never says who came back with Him (Peter, James and John) or where they were returning from (the mountain, Mark 9:2-9). The baker gets no context for who "they" are.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: In Mark 9:19, Jesus says "O unbelieving generation!" and "How long must I remain with you?" The text does not say who He is addressing. It could be the crowd, the scribes, the father or the disciples. The card's joke, "if I was one of those disciples, I'd be studying my sandals," points the rebuke at the disciples.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The question says "Right after calling them an unbelieving generation." "Them" points back to a card the baker can no longer see, and it never says who "them" is. It also carries over card 7's narrowing of who Jesus is speaking to, which the text leaves open.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The card says "this dad has been carrying this a LONG time." That comes from the father's answer "From childhood" in Mark 9:21, but the card cites only Mark 9:22.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the exact next word of Jesus' command: "never ___ him again." The choices are enter, find and follow. Picking between them depends on wording the baker hasn't seen, not on meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "find" is close in meaning to the right answer "enter." "Never find him again" also means the spirit never comes back to the boy, so a baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
